subject: AI & Agents
title: How AI Sees Images
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: How AI Sees Images.

hook.text: You see a golden retriever. A computer sees 786,432 numbers arranged in a grid.

buildup.text: Images are grids of pixels. Each pixel is just a color value — red, green, blue.

discovery.text: Convolutional neural networks scan small patches, detecting edges, then shapes, then objects.

twist.text: Change one pixel by a tiny amount and the model might call a panda a gibbon.

climax.text: AI vision now outperforms humans at reading X-rays, but it still trips on optical illusions.

quiz.question: What do convolutional neural networks detect first in an image?

details.summary: AI sees images as grids of numbers representing pixel brightness and color. Convolutional neural networks detect edges, shapes, and textures in layers, building up from simple features to complex recognition.
details.whyItMatters: Computer vision powers everything from face unlock to medical imaging to self-driving cars. Understanding how AI processes images reveals why it excels at some visual tasks and fails at others.
takeaways: AI processes images as numerical grids of pixel values
Convolutional layers detect progressively complex features
Lower layers find edges; higher layers recognize whole objects

faq.question: How does a neural network recognize objects in images?
faq.answer: Early layers detect simple features like edges and corners. Middle layers combine these into shapes and textures. Deep layers recognize whole objects by combining all lower-level features into complex patterns.

faq.question: Why does AI sometimes misidentify images?
faq.answer: AI relies on statistical patterns, not understanding. A slight change in lighting, angle, or a few altered pixels can fool it. Adversarial attacks exploit this by making tiny invisible changes that confuse the model.
